## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag should take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's CLI flag rules require an environment default for every flag added under `cli/`. This review found no other defect in the exclusion logic or its tests, which were read, not run.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py` that skips files whose base name matches any pattern while collecting paths, and logs each skipped path. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds five tests in `tests/test_main.py`, and adds a text fixture, `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` set and no `--exclude` argument, `args.exclude` is `[]` and no file is skipped, because the flag hard-codes `default=[]`. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5` (required reading per `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`) states: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable (for `--dry-run`, `ARCHIVE_DRY_RUN`), because CI sets options through the environment." — CI, which sets options through the environment, cannot configure exclusions, so its archives include files it meant to skip. — Fix: Take the default in `build_parser` from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, choose and document in `docs/flags.md` a separator for multiple globs, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the environment case.
